configuration: epoch2d/example_decks/window.deck at its shipped physics (256x256 cells over 1x1 m, simple_outflow in x, periodic in y, a moving window started at t = 0 travelling at 2e8 m/s, five cold macroparticles per cell loaded from a density profile that is 2 inside a slab centred at x = 1.31 m and |y - 0.5| < 0.2 and 1 elsewhere) run to 5 ns, half the deck's end time, with the dump cadence coarsened from 1e-10 s to 1e-9 s so the check writes 6 dumps rather than 101; graded: the electron number density in every one of the 65536 cells and the 257 x cell edges of the shifted grid, at dumps 1, 3 and 5
observable: the moving grid's origin and extent per graded dump (exact/near-exact agreement: a deterministic arithmetic recurrence, src/housekeeping/window.F90), and the loaded density profile's mean, excess-mass centroid and width along every spatial axis and its total excess mass -- moments of the profile rather than the raw per-cell density array
default_vs_upstream: 5 ns of the deck's 10 ns and dumps every 1e-9 s of 1e-10 s; SAB_T_END=10e-9 SAB_DT_SNAPSHOT=1e-10 restore
variant: the deck's explicit MPI rank layout, changed to a different valid decomposition of the same rank count (nprocx=2 to nprocx=1 for moving-window-1d; nprocx=2,nprocy=2 to nprocx=1,nprocy=4 for moving-window-2d; nprocx=2,nprocy=2,nprocz=1 to nprocx=1,nprocy=1,nprocz=4 for moving-window-3d), for the same reason as the injector checks: the electron load is a per-cell random draw from EPOCH's seeded stream, so a different rank layout is a correct, differently-ordered realisation of the same physics. The grid-origin/extent invariants are expected to stay exact under this variant (the window shift is a global arithmetic recurrence, not a per-rank random draw); the density-profile moments are expected to differ by the loader's finite-N realisation spread.
altbuild: run.sh altbuild builds the same pinned source and deck with epoch2d/Makefile's one gfortran FFLAGS line (line 72, -O3 -g -std=f2003) changed to -O0 -g -std=f2003 in the scratch build copy only, the same shipped flags at one lower optimisation level; a correct candidate could plausibly ship this build since it is the same compiler invocation the Makefile already offers at a different optimisation level. EPOCH's own MODE=debug profile was tried first and rejected: it aborts with SIGFPE inside Open MPI's own mpi_minimal_init (src/housekeeping/mpi_routines.F90:109) before any EPOCH arithmetic runs, on every dimension, so -ffpe-trap is not usable as this check's alternative build under this Open MPI.

altbuild.what: the same pinned source and deck on the same shipped gfortran build with epoch2d/Makefile's one FFLAGS line (line 72, -O3 -g -std=f2003) changed to -O0 -g -std=f2003 in the scratch build copy only: EPOCH's own MODE=debug profile aborts with SIGFPE inside Open MPI's own mpi_minimal_init (src/housekeeping/mpi_routines.F90:109) under this Open MPI before any EPOCH arithmetic runs, so this check uses the shipped build's exact flags at one lower optimisation level instead, dropping none of the compiler's own semantics and none of EPOCH's own code path.

warrant: Redesigned 2026-09-06 under the round-2 steward review (item 4) and the curator's option A: the previous pointwise policy compared the per-cell electron density and the grid coordinate arrays value-for-value. The electron load (a per-cell random draw from EPOCH's seeded KISS stream, 7842432 + rank; src/housekeeping/random_generator.f90, src/housekeeping/setup.F90) is subject to the same reordering argument as the injector checks: a differently parallelised, equally correct implementation can draw the same physical density profile in a different per-cell order. The moving window's shift, by contrast (src/housekeeping/window.F90), is a deterministic arithmetic recurrence timed off dt and window_v_x with no random draw in it at all, so the grid origin and extent stay graded exact/near-exact, unchanged in kind from the previous policy -- only wrapped in the invariants comparison alongside the redesigned density statistics so no check is added or removed. The redesigned density statistics are the profile's mean, its excess-mass centroid and width along every spatial axis (the blob the deck loads on top of the background, dens_blob over dens_bg within the deck's stated region) and its total excess mass: moments of the physical profile the loader is supposed to produce, not the raw per-cell occupancy a reordering can permute. A mis-scaled density stack, a shift schedule that loses or duplicates cells, or a loader that puts the blob in the wrong place all move these moments by O(1), while a legitimate reordering of the same per-cell draws does not.
